generation.domain: nonsingular real linear system; no exchanges; integer entries

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -6 & 6 & -6 \\ -2 & 5 & -2 & -2 \\ 2 & -5 & 0 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -6 & 6 & -6 \\ -2 & 5 & -2 & -2 \\ 2 & -5 & 0 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -2 \\ -2 & 5 & -2 & -2 \\ 2 & -5 & 0 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6 \\ 2 & -5 & 0 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6 \\ 0 & -1 & -4 & 10\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y+2z&=-2 \\ y+2z&=-6 \\ z&=-2\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=-2 \\ y&=-6-(2)(-2)=-2 \\ x&=-2-(-2)(-2)-(2)(-2)=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle -2,-2,-2\rangle$.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & -2 & -4 & 6 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & -7 \\ -2 & -1 & -5 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & -2 & -4 & 6 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & -7 \\ -2 & -1 & -5 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=-\frac{1}{2}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 & -7 \\ -2 & -1 & -5 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2-2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ -2 & -1 & -5 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-1R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -4\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y+2z&=-3 \\ y&=-1 \\ z&=-4\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=-4 \\ y&=-1-(0)(-4)=-1 \\ x&=-3-(1)(-1)-(2)(-4)=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 6,-1,-4\rangle$.

Consider the augmented matrix

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & 2 & 4 & -2 \\ -1 & 2 & 4 & -3 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & 2 & 4 & -2 \\ -1 & 2 & 4 & -3 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=-\frac{1}{2}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 & 4 & -3 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 5 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y-2z&=1 \\ y+2z&=-2 \\ z&=3\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=3 \\ y&=-2-(2)(3)=-8 \\ x&=1-(-1)(-8)-(-2)(3)=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle -1,-8,3\rangle$.

The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & 6 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 6 & -4 & 10\end{array}\right].
$$

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 6 & -4 & 10\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 10\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+4y-2z&=-4 \\ -x-y+3z&=-1 \\ -x-4y-5z&=0\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 4 & -2 & -4 \\ -1 & -1 & 3 & -1 \\ -1 & -4 & -5 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & 3 & -1 \\ -1 & -4 & -5 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ -1 & -4 & -5 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y-z&=-2 \\ y+2z&=-3 \\ z&=4\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=4 \\ y&=-3-(2)(4)=-11 \\ x&=-2-(2)(-11)-(-1)(4)=24.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 24,-11,4\rangle$.

$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -4 & -4 & 6 \\ -1 & 3 & 2 & -5 \\ 1 & -4 & -1 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & 3 & 2 & -5 \\ 1 & -4 & -1 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & -4 & -1 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y-2z&=3 \\ y&=-2 \\ z&=2\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=2 \\ y&=-2-(0)(2)=-2 \\ x&=3-(-2)(-2)-(-2)(2)=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 3,-2,2\rangle$.

$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & -6 & -5 & -7\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -6 & -5 & -7\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -1 & -5\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-1R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y-2z&=-1 \\ y&=1 \\ z&=3\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=3 \\ y&=1-(0)(3)=1 \\ x&=-1-(-2)(1)-(-2)(3)=7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 7,1,3\rangle$.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & 0 & -3 & -9 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ -1 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & 0 & -3 & -9 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ -1 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -1 & -3 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ -1 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & -4\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-z&=-3 \\ y-z&=1 \\ z&=1\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=1 \\ y&=1-(-1)(1)=2 \\ x&=-3-(0)(2)-(-1)(1)=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle -2,2,1\rangle$.
